lessons.title: Qu'est-ce qu'un texte?
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify different types of texts around them
materials: Various text examples (books, signs, labels, lists)

opening.activity: Look around classroom and point to different texts. Use gestures: point and say 'texte', 'livre', 'écrit'. Make discovery exciting!

mainActivity.activity: Text hunt around school - students find and point to different texts with teacher. Practice saying 'C'est un texte!' Use magnifying glasses for fun detective work.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may spot many texts, others just a few. Celebrate all discoveries equally.

closing.activity: Share discoveries in circle. Count how many different texts we found. Preview tomorrow's picture exploration.

decisionPoints: If students overwhelmed by text variety → Focus on just books and signs initially
If students want to read everything → Remind them we're just identifying texts today
If mobility needed → Make text hunt more active with walking and pointing
lessons.troubleshooting: If concept is too abstract, start with familiar books and gradually add other text types
lessons.realWorldConnection: Texts are all around us - signs help us find places, books tell stories, labels tell us what things are
lessons.progression: Foundation lesson - introduces the concept of texts everywhere

lessons.title: Images parlent aussi
lessons.oneGoal: Students understand that pictures give information just like words

opening.activity: Review yesterday's text hunt. Show book with only pictures. 'Est-ce que c'est un texte? Les images peuvent parler!'

mainActivity.activity: Explore wordless books together. Students 'read' pictures and tell what they see. Practice getting information from images without words.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may create elaborate stories, others just describe what they see. Both are perfect.

closing.activity: Share one thing they learned from pictures today. Introduce tomorrow's prediction activity.

decisionPoints: If students try to find hidden words → Celebrate picture-only texts as special and valuable
If students create long stories → Encourage but keep focus on information from pictures
If students say they can't read → Emphasize they ARE reading when they understand pictures
lessons.troubleshooting: If students insist pictures aren't 'real reading', use familiar signs and symbols as examples
lessons.realWorldConnection: Pictures help us understand when we can't read all the words - like bathroom signs or traffic lights
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by showing that texts include pictures that tell stories

lessons.title: Prédire avec les images
lessons.oneGoal: Students make predictions about stories using cover pictures

opening.activity: Review how pictures give information. Today we use pictures to guess what might happen. Model with familiar book cover.

mainActivity.activity: Show various book covers. Students make predictions based on pictures. Record predictions on chart. Use 'Je pense que...' sentence starter.
mainActivity.flexibility: Accept wild predictions - the goal is thinking about pictures, not being correct.

closing.activity: Choose one book to read tomorrow to check predictions. Students excited to see if they were right!

decisionPoints: If students make unrealistic predictions → Validate creativity while asking what picture clues they used
If students copy each other → Encourage but ask for different details they notice
If students worry about being wrong → Emphasize that all guesses help us think about stories
lessons.troubleshooting: If students can't make predictions, ask guided questions about what they see in pictures
lessons.realWorldConnection: We guess what might happen based on clues we see - like predicting weather from clouds
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by using pictures to guess what might happen

lessons.title: Écouter et découvrir
lessons.oneGoal: Students listen to a simple story and check their predictions

opening.activity: Review yesterday's predictions. Put on 'listening ears' to check if guesses were right.

mainActivity.activity: Read chosen story with expression and pictures. Stop periodically to check predictions. Celebrate both correct and incorrect predictions as good thinking.
mainActivity.flexibility: If story is too long, read part and continue tomorrow. If students are very engaged, finish the whole story.

closing.activity: Compare predictions to actual story. Discuss what surprised them. Preview tomorrow's retelling activity.

decisionPoints: If students disappointed about wrong predictions → Emphasize how predictions helped them think about story
If story too complex → Focus on pictures and simple events
If students want to interrupt → Allow some comments but keep story flowing
lessons.troubleshooting: If students can't follow story, use more gestures and pause for picture discussions
lessons.realWorldConnection: Sometimes our guesses are right, sometimes we learn something new - both help us understand better
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by checking if predictions were right

lessons.title: Reconter ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students retell story parts using simple words and gestures

opening.activity: Review yesterday's story briefly. 'Maintenant, nous recontons l'histoire ensemble!'

mainActivity.activity: Students retell story parts in sequence. Use props, gestures, and simple French words. Support with 'D'abord... Ensuite... Finalement...'
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may retell with lots of details, others just main events. Support all levels.

closing.activity: Whole group retelling with everyone contributing. Celebrate successful storytelling.

decisionPoints: If students mix up sequence → Use picture cues to help with order
If students use too much English → Model French words but accept mixed language
If students forget parts → Use prompting questions and pictures to support memory
lessons.troubleshooting: If retelling is too challenging, let students just point to pictures and say one word about each
lessons.realWorldConnection: We tell family about stories and movies we enjoyed - sharing helps us remember and enjoy more
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by retelling what they heard

lessons.title: Textes différents partout
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore different types of texts (signs, lists, letters)

opening.activity: Review that we've been reading stories. 'Il y a d'autres sortes de textes aussi!' Show variety of examples.

mainActivity.activity: Explore different text types - shopping lists, signs, letters, recipes. Discuss purpose of each type. Sort into categories.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may understand purposes quickly, others need more explanation. Use real examples they recognize.

closing.activity: Share different text types they found. Discuss which ones they see at home.

decisionPoints: If students confused by variety → Focus on just 2-3 clear examples first
If students excited about one type → Allow deeper exploration while covering others briefly
If students don't see purpose differences → Use concrete examples they can relate to
lessons.troubleshooting: If concept is too abstract, use texts from their daily life - lunch menus, name tags, etc.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Different texts help us in different ways - signs tell us where to go, lists help us remember things
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by discovering that not all texts are stories

lessons.title: Lire les indices
lessons.oneGoal: Students use context clues to understand unfamiliar words

opening.activity: Become detectives! When we don't know a word, we look for clues. Model with obvious picture-word connection.

mainActivity.activity: Practice finding clues in pictures and context when encountering unknown words. Use detective approach - what clues help us guess meaning?
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students natural detectives, others need more guidance. Celebrate all attempts at clue-finding.

closing.activity: Share best clues they found today. Remind them they can be word detectives with any text.

decisionPoints: If students guess wildly without using clues → Guide them to look at pictures and surrounding words
If students get frustrated with unknown words → Emphasize that good readers use clues, don't know every word
If students want exact definitions → Focus on general meaning from context rather than precision
lessons.troubleshooting: If clue-finding is too difficult, start with very obvious picture-word matches
lessons.realWorldConnection: We figure out new words by looking at pictures and other clues - like learning new things from context
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by learning strategies for unknown words

lessons.title: Questions importantes
lessons.oneGoal: Students ask 'who, what, where' questions about texts

opening.activity: Review being text detectives. 'Les détectives posent des questions!' Introduce question words with gestures.

mainActivity.activity: Practice asking 'Qui?' 'Quoi?' 'Où?' questions about familiar texts. Use question words cards as supports.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may generate many questions, others need prompting. Support question formation with sentence starters.

closing.activity: Share best questions they asked. Explain how questions help us understand stories better.

decisionPoints: If students struggle with question formation → Provide sentence frames and model questioning
If students ask very complex questions → Simplify to basic who/what/where format
If students answer instead of ask → Remind them we're practicing making questions today
lessons.troubleshooting: If questioning is too abstract, use familiar story and model each question type with clear examples
lessons.realWorldConnection: Asking questions helps us understand better - like asking questions when learning something new
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by actively questioning texts for understanding

lessons.title: Mes livres préférés
lessons.oneGoal: Students share favorite books and explain why they like them

opening.activity: Everyone has favorite books! Share teacher's favorite and explain why. Model simple reasons.

mainActivity.activity: Students share favorite books with partners and simple reasons why they like them. Use 'J'aime... parce que...' structure with supports.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students articulate detailed reasons, others just express like/dislike. Both are valuable.

closing.activity: Few students share favorites with whole class. Create class list of favorite books.

decisionPoints: If students can't explain why they like books → Offer simple reason prompts like 'funny' or 'pretty pictures'
If students say they don't have favorites → Help them think about books they remember or enjoyed
If students want to share many books → Encourage but help them choose one special favorite
lessons.troubleshooting: If students don't have book preferences yet, let them choose from classroom books they've enjoyed
lessons.realWorldConnection: Everyone has different favorite books and stories - just like having favorite foods or activities
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by expressing personal preferences about texts

lessons.title: Comparer les histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students compare two simple stories and find similarities/differences

opening.activity: Review favorite books. Today we compare two stories to see what's the same and different.

mainActivity.activity: Read/review two simple stories. Use chart to record what's the same and what's different. Support with visual comparisons.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may notice detailed similarities/differences, others just basic ones. All observations valuable.

closing.activity: Discuss what they learned from comparing stories. Some stories share ideas but tell them differently.

decisionPoints: If students focus only on differences → Guide them to look for similarities too
If students can't see comparisons → Use very obvious examples like character types or settings
If comparison is too complex → Focus on just one element like characters or main events
lessons.troubleshooting: If comparing is too abstract, use familiar stories with clear visual similarities
lessons.realWorldConnection: Some stories are similar to our own experiences - we can connect new stories to ones we know
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by analyzing relationships between texts

lessons.title: Textes informatifs
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore non-fiction texts about familiar topics

opening.activity: Review story books. 'Certains livres nous enseignent des choses vraies!' Show non-fiction examples.

mainActivity.activity: Explore simple non-fiction texts about animals, families, or familiar topics. Discuss how these teach real facts.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may grasp fiction/non-fiction distinction quickly, others need more concrete examples.

closing.activity: Share one new fact they learned today. Discuss difference between learning facts and enjoying stories.

decisionPoints: If students confused about real vs. story → Use clear examples like real animal photos vs. cartoon animals
If students prefer stories → Validate preference while showing value of learning facts
If content too complex → Focus on pictures and simple facts they can understand
lessons.troubleshooting: If fiction/non-fiction distinction is unclear, use familiar examples they know are real or pretend
lessons.realWorldConnection: Some books teach us true facts about the world - like how animals live or how things work
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by distinguishing fiction from non-fiction

lessons.title: Lire ensemble fort
lessons.oneGoal: Students participate in shared reading with expression

opening.activity: Review different types of texts. Today we read together with strong voices! Model expressive reading.

mainActivity.activity: Shared reading of familiar text with expression. Students join in on repeated phrases, practice different voices for characters.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may read along confidently, others just listen and join in occasionally.

closing.activity: Discuss how reading with expression makes stories more fun. Practice reading one sentence with different emotions.

decisionPoints: If students too shy to read aloud → Let them just listen or whisper along initially
If students very enthusiastic → Channel energy into expressive reading without overwhelming quiet students
If text too difficult → Focus on repetitive parts and familiar words students can join
lessons.troubleshooting: If shared reading is challenging, use very familiar songs or chants in text form
lessons.realWorldConnection: Reading aloud helps us understand and enjoy stories more - like how family reads bedtime stories
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by practicing reading skills together

lessons.title: Création de questions
lessons.oneGoal: Students create their own questions about a familiar text

opening.activity: Review asking questions about texts. Today students become the question creators! Model making questions.

mainActivity.activity: Students create their own questions about familiar text using question word prompts. Support with sentence frames and encouragement.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may create many questions, others need lots of support. Celebrate all question-making attempts.

closing.activity: Students ask their questions to partners. Celebrate being good questioners who help others think.

decisionPoints: If students struggle creating questions → Provide question stems and help them complete
If students create questions too complex → Guide them toward simpler, answerable questions
If students copy each other's questions → Validate similarities and encourage different question words
lessons.troubleshooting: If question creation is too difficult, let students choose from pre-made question options to ask
lessons.realWorldConnection: Good readers ask questions to understand better - questioning shows we're thinking about what we read
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by becoming active questioners of texts

lessons.title: Portfolio de lecture
lessons.oneGoal: Students compile favorite texts and explain their reading journey

opening.activity: Look back at all the texts and skills from this unit. 'Regardez tout ce que nous avons appris sur les textes!'

mainActivity.activity: Students create reading portfolio with favorite texts, pictures of learning activities, and simple reflections on their growth.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may want elaborate portfolios, others simple collections. Support all approaches.

closing.activity: Students share one thing they learned about texts. Celebrate growth as text explorers and readers.

decisionPoints: If students overwhelmed by portfolio creation → Help them choose just 2-3 meaningful items
If students don't see their progress → Point out specific skills they've gained during unit
If students want to include everything → Help them select most important or favorite examples
lessons.troubleshooting: If reflection is too abstract, use concrete examples of what they can do now that they couldn't before
lessons.realWorldConnection: We can look back and see how much we've learned - like looking at baby photos to see how we've grown
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by reflecting on learning and growth

lessons.title: Explorateurs de genres
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore poetry, fairy tales, and other genres through play

opening.activity: Review all different text types learned. Today explore special kinds of stories - poetry, fairy tales, etc.

mainActivity.activity: Playful exploration of different genres through listening, acting, and simple identification games. Focus on enjoyment over analysis.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let students gravitate toward genres that interest them while ensuring exposure to variety.

closing.activity: Share which genre was most interesting today. Discuss how many different ways there are to tell stories.

decisionPoints: If students prefer familiar story types → Validate preferences while gently introducing new genres
If students confused by genre differences → Focus on obvious distinctions like rhyming vs. non-rhyming
If students very engaged with one genre → Allow deeper exploration while touching on others
lessons.troubleshooting: If genre concept is too complex, focus on obvious features like 'stories that rhyme' vs. 'regular stories'
lessons.realWorldConnection: There are many different kinds of stories and texts to enjoy - like different types of games or music
lessons.progression: Extension - applies text exploration skills to new genres

lessons.title: Détectives de mots
lessons.oneGoal: Students hunt for familiar words in new texts

opening.activity: Return to detective theme! Today hunt for words we know in new places. Model finding familiar word in new text.

mainActivity.activity: Word hunting game in new texts - students search for and collect familiar words they can recognize and understand.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some may find many words, others just a few. Celebrate all discoveries and growing word knowledge.

closing.activity: Share word hunting successes. Discuss how knowing some words helps us read new things.

decisionPoints: If students can't find familiar words → Provide texts with obvious high-frequency words they know
If students want to sound out everything → Encourage but keep focus on recognizing familiar words
If word hunting takes too long → Set timer and celebrate whatever they find in time limit
lessons.troubleshooting: If students frustrated by unknown words, remind them they're looking for words they already know
lessons.realWorldConnection: Finding words we know helps us read new things - like recognizing friend's names in new places
lessons.progression: Extension - deepens word recognition skills through games

lessons.title: Théâtre des histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students act out favorite stories to show comprehension

opening.activity: Review favorite stories from unit. Today we become actors and show stories with our bodies and voices!

mainActivity.activity: Students choose familiar stories to act out in small groups. Focus on showing understanding through movement and simple dialogue.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some groups may create elaborate performances, others simple scenes. Support all levels of dramatic expression.

closing.activity: Mini performances for class. Celebrate how acting helps us understand and remember stories better.

decisionPoints: If students too shy for performance → Start with just movements or let them be props/scenery
If students get too excited → Channel energy into character actions while maintaining focus
If groups can't agree on story → Help them choose or suggest familiar group favorites
lessons.troubleshooting: If acting is too challenging, let students just show one scene or character action from story
lessons.realWorldConnection: Acting out stories helps us understand characters and events - like how we act out games we play
lessons.progression: Extension - demonstrates understanding through creative expression

lessons.title: Bibliothécaires experts
lessons.oneGoal: Students recommend books to classmates based on interests

opening.activity: Discuss how librarians help people find good books. Today students become book experts who help friends!

mainActivity.activity: Students interview classmates about interests, then recommend books from classroom library. Practice giving simple reasons for recommendations.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students natural matchmakers, others need guidance. Support all attempts at thoughtful matching.

closing.activity: Share successful recommendations made today. Discuss how helping others find good books makes reading more fun.

decisionPoints: If students recommend same books to everyone → Help them think about different interests and preferences
If students can't explain recommendations → Provide simple reason prompts like 'funny' or 'has animals'
If students disagree with recommendations → Validate that people like different things
lessons.troubleshooting: If recommendation process is complex, let students just share favorite books with reasons they like them
lessons.realWorldConnection: Librarians and friends help us find books we'll enjoy - sharing good books spreads the fun of reading
lessons.progression: Extension - uses text knowledge to help others

lessons.title: Textes de chez nous
lessons.oneGoal: Students explore texts from their own cultures and families

opening.activity: Discuss how every family and culture has special stories and texts. Invite sharing about texts from home.

mainActivity.activity: Students share texts, stories, or traditions from their families/cultures. Celebrate diversity and different ways of telling stories.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may have lots to share, others little. Support all levels of cultural connection.

closing.activity: Reflect on how many different types of stories and texts exist in our classroom community.

decisionPoints: If students don't have cultural texts to share → Help them think about family stories or traditions
If students share very personal stories → Support with sensitivity and respect
If students feel left out → Emphasize that all families have stories, even simple everyday ones
lessons.troubleshooting: If students don't connect with cultural aspect, focus on any family stories or special books from home
lessons.realWorldConnection: Every family and culture has special stories and texts - like recipes, songs, or bedtime stories
lessons.progression: Extension - connects text exploration to personal identity

lessons.title: Célébration de lecteurs
lessons.oneGoal: Students celebrate their growth as text explorers and readers

opening.activity: Look back at journey from Lesson 1 to now. 'Vous êtes maintenant des explorateurs de textes experts!'

mainActivity.activity: Celebration of reading growth with sharing of portfolios, presentation of certificates, and reflection on favorite discoveries.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let students highlight what they're most proud of learning during the unit.

closing.activity: Final circle: each student completes 'Je suis un explorateur de textes parce que...' Group celebration photo.

decisionPoints: If students don't feel like 'real' readers → Emphasize all the text skills they've developed
If students want to keep exploring → Encourage continued text exploration in free time
If celebration feels overwhelming → Keep it simple with just sharing and recognition
lessons.troubleshooting: If students don't recognize their growth, use specific examples of skills they've gained during unit
lessons.realWorldConnection: Readers celebrate discovering new worlds through texts - every text they explore makes them stronger readers
lessons.progression: Extension - culminates unit with reflection on reading journey
